context: The box on the right defines d as the left subtree height minus the right subtree height and requires |d| ≤ 1 at every node. Here d is a height difference, distinct from node degree. With height measured in edges, a leaf has height 0 and an empty subtree has height −1.
description: The tree on the left has four levels and 8 nodes without value labels. The root's left child has just one left leaf and an empty right subtree. It is labeled d = 1.

The root's right child has two children. Its left child is an internal node with two leaves, and its right child is itself a leaf. Thus the root's right child is labeled d = 1, and its left child is labeled d = 0. All four leaves have empty left and right subtrees and are labeled d = 0.

frames.explanation: The root's left subtree has height 1 and its right subtree has height 2, so the root is labeled d = −1. The subtree heights at every other node also differ by at most 1, so the entire tree is balanced.
frames.title: Balanced binary tree: subtree heights differ by at most 1 at every node

result: Check every node for balance. The height difference at the root alone is insufficient.
summary: Although this tree is asymmetric, every node satisfies the balance condition.
title: Balanced binary tree: subtree heights differ by at most 1 at every node
